title: Impact of Fintech Adoption, Green Innovation, and Organizational Financial Literacy on Sustainable Performance of SMEs Through Circular Economy Practices
content:
ABSTRACT

The world is facing an alarming challenge of environmental threats due to overproduction and overconsumption of scarce resources. Manufacturing SMEs are considered the backbone of this problem. SMEs are also considered key actors in promoting a circular economy and sustainable performance (SP). This study aims to investigate the direct impact of fintech adoption (FA), green innovation (GI), access to finance (AF), and organizational financial literacy (OFL) on the sustainable performance (SP) of SMEs operating in Pakistan. The study further aims to investigate the indirect relationship via circular economy practices (CEP) between independent and dependent variables. The researcher dispensed closed-ended structured questionnaires to managers and owners of SMEs in Pakistan. The researcher employed a non-probability, purposive sampling technique to select respondents. Eight hypotheses were formulated to test the study's model. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and structural equation modelling (SEM) in Smart-PLS were used for data analysis. Seven out of eight hypotheses were accepted after making an empirical analysis. The results reveal that SMEs following CEP tend to enjoy both competitive advantage and environmental benefits. The study also reveals that financially enlightened managerial staff are inclined to make informed and environmentally friendly decisions. The study has theoretical implications for the Natural Resource Based View (NRBV) theory. The study also guides SME owners and managers to adopt technology 14.0 (fintech) along with CEP to achieve sustainable performance (SP). It also guides policy regulators to prioritize SMEs for CEP to achieve environmental benefits. SMEs are adopting modern world concepts to ensure their survival and growth in the industry. At the same time, they're under pressure from stakeholders due to their environmental effects. The study aims to assess the impact of modern world concepts (FA, GI) in conjunction with the circular economy (CEP) to achieve both competitive and environmental benefits.
